evidence.positive: Against the running build (ecefa57d2, Mayo tenant mayo-mayo): staged a 130 kg patient via the admin API, gave an earlier 3 g IV cefazolin bolus 5 min after operation start, ran /api/cds/medication-selection for m-cefazolin (real redose firing, a-antibiotic-early-redose recorded CRCL null) and documented 2 g IV via /api/patient/.../medication-administration. Reshaped that real firing by SQL into the pre-fix shape (rule_identifier w-default-dose-adjustment, 3 g default on INTRAVENOUS and INTRAOSSEOUS copied verbatim from a real overweight first-dose firing) and let the app's own evaluator score it via POST /api/firings/{id}/seen: default-dose compliant=false (the bug). Deleted the 240 row from mayo-mayo.databasechangelog, restarted the container; Liquibase re-ran it (databasechangelog row re-added EXECUTED 17:13:06). DB after: route_default_dose_override = {INTRAVENOUS:{doseAmount:2.0,doseUnits:g,calculatedDoseAmount:'2',calculatedDoseUnits:g,calculatedLabel:'2 g',rawLabel:'2 g',defaultOption:true,...}, same for INTRAOSSEOUS}, compliance_results default-dose compliant=true, last_modified_date 17:13:05. Two in-scope clones also rescored: CRCL exactly 50 with 2000 mg given -> 2 g / true; in scope but 3 g given -> 2 g / false. Then re-POSTed the same 2 g administration through the medication-administration endpoint (afterCommit evaluateComplianceOnMedicationAdministration) and the verdict stayed true, so the stored default and verdict agree (AC 3). Recomputing the two clones via /seen also kept 2000 mg -> true and 3 g -> false.
evidence.negative: Seven out-of-scope rows, all in pre-fix shape (w-default-dose-adjustment, 3 g default) and scored by the app before the re-run, were untouched by the Liquibase re-run (default still 3 g, verdict unchanged): real overweight first dose with no earlier bolus (false stays false); real 80 kg NORMAL redose (false); clone with early-redose CRCL 40 (false); clone with CRCL 49.9 (false); clone whose administration is 20 mL (true stays true); clone with dose_amount NULL (true); clone already storing a 2 g default (2 g / true, left alone). Other-tenant check: the same pre-fix-shaped firing in demo-demo (real redose, reshaped identically) stayed 3 g / false and demo-demo.databasechangelog shows 240 as MARK_RAN (re-added at 17:13:04 after its row was also deleted); mgb-mgh and mgb-icsnh show MARK_RAN from the original boot.
evidence.red_check: Data flip of the AC-3 failure mode: after the rewrite, set the in-scope firing's route_default_dose_override back to the 3 g shape by SQL (verdict true but default not rewritten), then re-POSTed the identical 2 g administration with selectedIndication=OR3069-RED-CHECK-3G-DEFAULT as a marker. The app's compliance recompute reverted the verdict to compliant=false (red), and the log shows 'Dose data: MedicationDosingDTO(... selectedIndication=OR3069-RED-CHECK-3G-DEFAULT ...)' for exactly that request. Reverted by executing the shipped changeset SQL body (extracted from the XML) against mayo-mayo via psql: default back to 2 g, verdict true, all other fixture rows unchanged; re-POSTed again without the marker and the verdict stayed true.

caveats: The current build no longer writes w-default-dose-adjustment firings for cefazolin, so the pre-fix rows were real app-generated firings reshaped by SQL (rule identifier and the 3 g default JSON copied from a real first-dose firing); the 3 g and 2 g JSON shapes themselves were produced by the app.
Fixture firings had evaluation_mode INTERACTIVE (admin-driven selection), not Mayo's SILENT; the changeset does not filter on mode.
The earlier-bolus time boundary (1 minute before operation start) was not probed at the edge; the earlier bolus was 5 minutes after start.
Changeset 241 (OR-2941, same SQL for later firings) was executed in mayo-mayo at boot but was not separately exercised here.
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '2s' was not exercised under lock contention.

automation.assessment: No existing test covers this changeset; Liquibase data migrations have no in-repo test harness (schema in tests comes from entities, not the changelogs). The scope predicate has several boundaries (redose detection, CrCl 50, g/mg units, all-routes 3 g) that a SQL-level fixture test could lock in, but the changeset is one-shot per tenant and already executed, so the value is low after deploy.
proposed_tests: Testcontainers Postgres test that creates a mayo-mayo schema via the tenant changelog, seeds the ten fixture shapes used here (in-scope 2 g, CRCL 50/49.9/40, mg units, mL units, null dose, first dose, normal weight, already 2 g), re-runs changeset 240 and asserts the rewritten default JSON and verdicts; mark it supplemental and skip if the team keeps migrations manual-only.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A real Mayo overweight 2 g cefazolin redose firing, reshaped to the pre-fix 3 g default and scored non-compliant by the app, was rewritten to a 2 g default and rescored compliant when Liquibase re-ran changeset 240, and the app's compliance recompute on the same administration kept it compliant.
Negative: First-dose, normal-weight, CrCl 40 and 49.9, mL-unit, null-dose and already-2 g firings were left untouched, and the same firing in demo-demo stayed 3 g with the changeset marked ran there.
Red check: Setting the stored default back to 3 g while leaving the verdict and recomputing through the medication-administration endpoint flipped the verdict back to non-compliant, and re-applying the shipped SQL restored 2 g and compliant.

Automation: No harness exists for tenant data changesets; a Testcontainers fixture test is proposed but low value for a one-shot migration.
